Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:81: The third gate, on the proper timing for union
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:82: Know that according to each person's food, so will the nourished body be. And by way of investigation it is known that the animal from which musk is drawn feeds on spikenard. Now, the Name, blessed be He, in all His ways is just; He commanded that animals be slaughtered for food — and why is this necessary? Would it not be better for us to be nourished by kinds of fruit and produce, rather than to shed the blood of animals and beasts and cause them great suffering?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:83: Know that these are foundations of the world, that the Name, blessed be He, does good to every creature and has mercy on His creatures, and of this it is said (Psalms 145:9), "the LORD is good to all." One who knows this verse knows that the slaughter of living creatures and their being eaten by people is for the good of the living creatures themselves, and is compassion and mercy toward them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:84: I shall explain: it is known that all food a person eats goes into the stomach, and from there descends to the upper intestines, and from there the liver draws out the good, choicest, richest, purest, and cleanest part of that food, and pushes the rest to the lower intestines, from which it exits through excretion; and that which the liver draws out, it cooks again, and it returns, in each organ, according to the kind of that organ, through a third cooking, and becomes flesh in flesh, fat in fat, sinew in sinew, and bone in bone, for from it the body is nourished. If so, we find that this animal that was slaughtered was slaughtered for its own good, since it rose from the level of an animal's body to the level of a human body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:85: This is the manner of the four compositions of the lower world, which are minerals, plants, and speaking living beings. For minerals draw and are nourished from the four elements, and plants are nourished from the four elements and from minerals; and non-speaking living beings are nourished from plants and minerals and the four elements; and the speaking living being makes use of the non-speaking living beings, of plants, of minerals, and of the four elements. So everything proceeds from elevation to elevation until the cycle turns forward and backward, and of this it is said, "the LORD is good to all" — from the elements it rises to a level above them, which is minerals; and minerals rise to a level above them, which is growing plants; and from plants they rise above them, which are non-speaking living beings that move and grow and are composed of the four elements; and from non-speaking living beings they rise to a level greater than them, which are speaking living beings, who possess the power of speech, the power of movement, the power of growth, and the power of composition from the four elements. If so, we find that all things become food for others in order to raise them to a great elevation above their own level.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:86: After this introduction, know that since blood is the nourishment of the body and what refines the body, and blood is, according to the nature of the food from which it is made, thick or turbid — if the food is clean, pure, and refined, the blood will be likewise. Therefore He, blessed be He, separated us, in His holy Torah, from several forbidden foods that He forbade to us: some that dull the heart, like milk and blood [together]; some that harden the face, like predatory beasts, birds, and animals; some that close the doors of understanding and wisdom, like the hare, the rock badger, the pig, and their like; and some that engender several harsh and evil illnesses, like the creeping things of the earth and water. In sum, of all of them He said (Leviticus 11:43), "do not make your souls detestable." He has thus informed us that all these things are loathsome and disgusting and produce bad blood, prone to several punishments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:87: Now, if so, when it is said that a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, food too is included in this sanctification, for it is fitting for a person to eat proper and fitting foods, balanced between cold and heat, and that they be from things that produce clean, pure, refined blood — since that blood is destined to be transformed into the substance of the seed, and it is destined to be the foundation and building material for the child born from that union. For if the food were bad, turbid, and thick, the drop too would be thick, filthy, and turbid; if so, we find that food, for the formation of a person, is a preparation for his being wise or foolish, righteous or wicked.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:88: I shall hand you a great key: know that since the matter is as we have said, the Name, blessed be He, joined, in His holy Torah, the portion of "a woman who conceives" to [the portion of] forbidden foods, saying (Leviticus 11:47), "to distinguish between the impure and the pure" etc., and adjacent to it, "a woman who conceives"; and He joined, on the other side, the portion of tzara'at [skin afflictions]. These three portions contain wondrous secrets, with the portion of "a woman who conceives" in the middle, to inform us that if a person separates himself from bad foods, he will have fitting, holy, and pure children; but if not, tzara'at afflictions arise upon them from the side of the drop of seed that came from those detestable foods. Therefore this comes to inform you that a person must also sanctify himself with fitting foods close to the time of relations, so that the seed be clean and pure and balanced between north and south, as we have said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:89: Now, we have informed you that according to the food, so will the blood produced be; and according to the blood, so will the seed be; and according to the seed, so will the child born from it be. And you already know what we have said, that an eagle is not born from a horse, nor lentils from wheat; likewise we say that from a turbid, evil drop, only detestable and disgusting blood is born, as is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:90: Now, we have informed you in this way of the proper manner of food, and it is fitting for us to tell you that of proper food one need not take an amount sufficient to fill the body, but only a moderate amount that nature can grind, so it may quickly be transformed into clean, pure blood — for when food is excessive in the stomach, even if it is of fitting things, its excess will cause it not to be ground and it will spoil in the stomach, and it will come back worse and filthier than if it had been of coarse and bad things. Therefore it is fitting to be careful about the quantity of food just as one is careful about the actual substance of the food. Guard, then, this great principle, which is prepared from the side of food toward the side of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:91: The fourth gate, on the intent of union
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:92: What our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma 29a) is a great secret: "the fantasy of transgression is harder than the transgression itself." I shall now illuminate your eyes with matters that are among the depths of the world, hidden in several inner chambers. Know that the Name, blessed be He, is a God of knowledge; He established His works with complete wisdom, and gave to each of the world's natures its own particular action assigned to it as a fixed charge, without change, except by way of miracle. Now, He placed a power in a person's imagination to beget something resembling the thing he imagines, and this we know also from the side of nature. When a person unites with his wife, if his imagination and thoughts are occupied with wisdom, understanding, and good, fitting character traits, that imagination present in his thoughts has the power, without doubt, to imprint its form upon the drop of seed just as he was imagining at the time of union — this is the secret of (Genesis 30:37), "and Jacob took for himself rods of fresh poplar" etc., and it says, "and the flocks became warm before the rods" etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:93: And our Sages of blessed memory said in Berachot (cf. 20a; see also Bava Metzia 84a): Rabbi Yochanan used to go and sit at the gates of the immersion pool, saying, when the daughters of Israel go up and come from the river, let them look at me, so that they will have children as handsome as I. Contemplate this vision, for this pious man informed us that when a woman thinks of his beauty as she rises from immersion and then unites with her husband, she binds the form of the child according to the image she imagines; if so, we find that imagination is a great cause, and that fantasy and thought cause the child and his qualities to be as we have explained. Behold, that fantasy and thought cause the child to be righteous or wicked, just as food causes it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:94: Every person must cleanse his thoughts and fantasies and purify them at the time of relations, and not think of a matter of transgression or lewdness, but only of holy things; he should think of the pure righteous, men of knowledge, intellect, and wisdom, for those thoughts will settle upon the seed and imprint it in their form at the time of relations. Likewise his wife's thought — that she be gladdened with things that gladden the heart, so that she too agree with pure and clean thoughts, and both be unified in the matter of the mitzvah — for then their thought will be bound as one and the Shechinah will rest between them, and they will beget a son according to the pure form they imagined.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:95: Do not be astonished at this matter, for it is a simple nature in the eyes of the sages of investigation, that according to the thought and fantasy that passes over the heart of a person and his wife at the time of their union, so will the child be prepared and found to be, whether good or bad. And they have already brought (cf. Bereshit Rabbah 73:10) the story of that noblewoman who bore a black son, though she and the king were both very fair-skinned; and the king thought to kill her, until a certain sage came and said to him, perhaps she fantasized at the time of relations about a black man — and they investigated and found black figures on the decorations of that room in which she had relations, and she said that she had been gazing at those figures and fantasizing about them at the time of union. This is like the matter of the rods.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:96: Do not be astonished, for something greater than this is known from nature: a person bitten by a rabid dog, who falls ill with the illness known from that bite — from that very imagination which he imagines in his mind, one cannot bring water before him, for immediately he imagines that there are rabid dogs in it; and even in his urine, images of very fierce dogs will appear, since from the abundance of his fantasy and confusion his urine bears the marks of his fantasies and confusions. Understand this very well, and see how far the power of imagination and fantasy at the time of relations reaches.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:97: In sum: if a person fantasizes about good and pure things, that good fantasy settles upon the drop of seed, and the child will be imprinted with the form of that fantasy, and will be destined to be completely righteous; of him it is said (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the womb" etc. — for truly, before his form was made, the good fantasy was ready to imprint it, and then the Shechinah joins with the pure thought, as our Sages of blessed memory said (Kiddushin 40a), a good thought — the Holy One, blessed be He, joins it to the deed. But if a person thinks of a matter of transgression and ugliness, the child is founded upon a foundation of wickedness and ugliness and is destined to be a filthy wicked person; of him it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:98: I must arouse you to a great principle found in the Torah and in the words of our Sages of blessed memory: "God settles the solitary in a home" (Psalms 68:7), and they said, whoever marries a woman for the sake of beauty — a new [child] enters and a new [child] leaves, and the sword consumes him, as it is said (Hosea 5:7), "they have betrayed the LORD, for they have begotten strange children." The great secret here is that when he marries a woman for the sake of beauty, his union is not for the sake of Heaven, for he is truly fantasizing about her form in a physical manner and not thinking with a pure, supernal thought; and the son born from that fantasy is a foreign, strange son, of whom it is said, "for they have begotten strange children," and the Name has no portion in him — they are found to be traitors, and the Shechinah departs from between them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:99: I have come to arouse you to a great principle: know that this is why the portion of the stubborn and rebellious son and the portion of the hanged man were placed adjacent to the portion of the beautiful captive woman — for from a woman taken captive in war, a righteous man will not emerge, since the intent was only for beauty and lust, and stubborn and bitter sons emerge from her, fit for the four death penalties of the court. Know that it was not for nothing that the matter of Tamar and Absalom happened to David, for both were children of a beautiful captive; for all this is caused by fantasy resembling that image. This, then, is what we have aroused you to in this chapter regarding the intent of union, thought, and fantasy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:100: I wish to arouse you to a great principle, and I shall hand you a great gift regarding the secret of thought, how it acts upon the form of the matter it receives from it. Now, our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma 29a), "the fantasy of transgression is harder than the transgression itself," and elsewhere they said (Kiddushin 40a), "an evil thought — the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join it to the deed, except for idolatry," as it is said (Ezekiel 14:5), "in order to seize the house of Israel by their heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:101: I shall now illuminate your eyes regarding matters that come sealed in the Gemara. Our Sages of blessed memory said (Vayikra Rabbah 16:4; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10): Ben Azzai was sitting and studying, and fire was blazing around him; and Rabbi Eliezer was sitting and expounding, and rays shone from him like the rays of our teacher Moses, peace be upon him (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, ch. 2). You need to know that all these matters have a single intent, and I shall explain: a spring of water, when it is drawn from a high place to a low place, has the power to raise those waters to another high place, corresponding to the height of the source from which the water issues. Likewise it is known to one who fears Heaven that a person's thought is from the source of the intellectual soul, which is drawn from the supernal beings, and thought has the power to spread and rise and reach up to its point of origin; and upon reaching the source, it attaches itself to the supernal secret from which it was drawn, and it and that source become one thing. And when the thought returns, drawn from above to below, everything becomes like a single line, and that supernal light is drawn downward; and then the bright light is drawn and spreads in that place where the possessor of the thought sits. So too the early pious ones would attach their thought to the supernal beings and draw the supernal light downward, and through this things would increase and multiply according to the power of the thought — this is the secret of the oil of Elisha, peace be upon him, and the jar of flour and jug of oil of Elijah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:102: Since this is so, our Sages of blessed memory needed to say that when a person unites with his wife and his thought is attached to the supernal beings, that thought draws supernal light downward, and it rests upon that drop upon which he intends and fantasizes, like the matter of the jug [of oil]; and that drop is found bound forever to the bright light. This is the secret of "before [I formed you in the womb]" (Jeremiah 1:5) etc. — since the bright light was already bound to that righteous man's drop at the time of union, because the thought was attached to the supernal beings and drew the bright light. Understand this very well, and you will understand from it a great secret regarding "the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob" — for it is said there that at the time they were occupied with eating, drinking, marital relations, and other bodily matters, what would be [the status] of it [i.e., of the divine attachment]? And the answer was that even in all their bodily affairs, their whole intent was for the sake of Heaven, and their thought never separated from the supernal light even for a single moment; and through this Jacob merited to beget twelve tribes, all of them completely righteous and perfect, fit to be like the patterns of the orders of the world, bearers of the vessels of the LORD, since their thought did not separate from the supernal light even at the time of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:103: Therefore Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 3:6), "in all your ways know Him" — and this "knowing" is the joining of the intellectual soul, its attachment to the supernal light; and one is not called to "know" a certain thing until the intellect attaches itself to the object of its understanding.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:104: Now that we have informed you of this, consider why "the fantasy of transgression is harder than the transgression itself" — for when a person thinks of matters of wickedness and filth, his thought attaches itself in its filth to the supernal beings, and his soul is thereby obligated toward Heaven, since it becomes defiled by contact; but were he to commit a transgression below without this contact reaching Heaven, its judgment would be lighter upon him than an evil fantasy, which comes close to "cutting the plantings" [heresy]. From this you will understand the secret of "the fantasy of transgression is harder than the transgression itself": one who fantasizes about transgression at the time of relations — that filthy thought settles upon the drop, and establishes from it a foundation of wickedness, injustice, and filth, and it is called "strange." From this you will understand the deed of that pious man who sat at the gates of the immersion pool, so that their [the women's] thought and fantasy be attached to his form, his form being bound to the supernal beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:105: We shall further inform you of another matter regarding thought — although it does not pertain to the intent of union, nevertheless it is useful to know for oneself and for others. It is that when holy, pious men attached their thought to the supernal beings, whatever they thought about at that hour would come to be, whether good or bad — this is what is meant by (Berachot 58a), "he set his eyes upon him and he became a heap of bones," and it is written in Ta'anit (24a) in that beraita, "return to your dust," and so it was; and what is said (Chagigah 5b), "any place upon which the Sages set their eyes, either death or poverty [ensues]." And from this matter is the secret of prayer and of the sacrifices, which is the secret of attachment to the supernal beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:106: From this matter came the power of that accursed wicked Balaam, of whom they used to say (Numbers 22:6), "whomever you bless [and whomever you curse]" etc.; therefore he wished to gaze intently upon Israel, in order to be able to attach his thought to the supernal beings and draw down upon them an evil thought — therefore it says (ibid. 24:2), "and Balaam lifted up his eyes" etc.; and therefore he needed to be precise (ibid. 23:13), "come, please, with me to another place from which you may see them" etc. — for the wicked one needed to gaze at what his intent was directed toward, whether for good or for evil, and he would attach his thought above and draw supernal power to whomever he intended and gazed upon — this is the matter of (ibid. 24:4), "who sees the vision of Shaddai, falling down, with opened eyes." Therefore the wicked one intended to build seven altars, with a bull and a ram on each, in order to draw into himself all the [supernal] powers and bring them near to his thought, in order to fulfill his desire and his evil will in whatever he craved. Therefore it says (ibid. 23:14), "and he took him to the field of the watchers," for the wicked one was watching them in order to draw his evil thought upon them. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows all thoughts, knew his evil thought, and did not permit it to the will of the wicked Balaam. Understand this well, and know how far the power of thought reaches.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:107: Now that we have informed you of these sealed secrets, we must inform you of the secret of the next way, properly, with the help of the LORD.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:108: The fifth gate, on the manner of union
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:109: It is known that every pious and modest man, when he speaks, speaks only in a soft language, a gentle tongue, and with calm spirit, and does not speak of great matters; and when he walks, he walks with a bent posture and lowered head, and so in all his conduct. The wicked person is, in all his ways, the opposite of this. You should consider that since matters which have no disgrace in themselves are disgraceful when done disgracefully among people, all the more so is there disgrace in a disgraceful organ and a disgraceful deed. Therefore, whenever a man unites with a woman, he should not be lighthearted or speak vain and deceptive words, and should not take his mind lightly toward the woman, nor engage in excessive idle talk with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:110: Therefore you should first draw her in with words that draw her heart, settle her mind, and gladden her, so that her mind be bound to your mind and her intent to your intent. Say to her words, some that draw her toward desire, love, and goodwill, and some that draw her toward the fear of Heaven, piety, and modesty; and tell her stories of pious and modest women, how fitting and worthy children — masters of Torah, awe, and instruction — emerged from them, such as the story of Kimchit, who merited seven sons, all of whom served as High Priest, and our Sages of blessed memory asked her by what merit she achieved this, and she said to them, even the beams of my house never saw the hair of my head in my days (Yoma 47a) — and all this she attained as reward for her modesty, piety, and the uprightness of her deeds. And converse with her in the middle of the night, or close to the last third, for it was taught in Berachot (3a), in the third watch a baby nurses from its mother's breast and a woman converses with her husband.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:111: In sum: when you examine yourself and see that you are fit for relations, examine your wife's mind as well, and let it agree with your mind; and when you unite, do not hasten to arouse desire in her, so that her mind be settled. And from all the matters we have informed you in the preceding words, and in this manner, you can infer several matters we have not mentioned from those we have mentioned, and you should include all of them together. And from your own understanding you will grasp the manner of conduct proper for a person at the time of relations, more than any modesty you observe regarding all your temperaments in eating, drinking, and worldly conduct — for according to the modesty and thought you exercise at the time of union, so will the form settle upon the drop of seed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:112: This is the secret of (Genesis 25:19), "these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham" etc. — meaning, after the Holy One, blessed be He, told him, "Sarah your wife shall bear you a son," Abraham had, at the time of union, an intent surpassing all his other good qualities, attaching his thought to the supernal beings and intending to beget a son who would be worthy of what the Holy One, blessed be He, had told him. This is the secret of "Abraham begot Isaac" — he intended to beget a son who would be completely righteous like himself. This is the secret of "Abraham begot" — our Sages of blessed memory said (Bereshit Rabbah 63:1), a righteous man, the son of a righteous man; and the power of his righteousness reached such a degree that the Holy One, blessed be He, testified that there was no blemish in him, neither inside nor out — this is the secret of (Genesis 22:2), "and offer him there as a burnt offering" — and you already know that it was not fitting for there to be a blemish in something offered upon the altar. Understand this great vision. And you already know that the burnt offering is a most holy sacrifice (Zevachim 5:5), and it comes for a sinful thought of the heart (Vayikra Rabbah 7:3) and for perceptible sins (Yoma 36a); therefore it requires flaying and dissection, and Isaac is called "a perfect burnt offering" (Bereshit Rabbah 64:3) — and all this Abraham caused at the time of union, when he intended purely for the sake of Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:113: So too it is with the other pious men of heart, that when they intend for the sake of the mitzvah, attaching their thought to the supernal beings at the time of union, they beget children fit for holiness, purity, and piety. Therefore the scroll of Ruth had to write (Ruth 4:18), "these are the generations of Peretz: Peretz begot Chetzron" — since Peretz, a completely righteous man, likewise intended to beget a righteous son like himself. This is the secret of "Peretz begot Chetzron," and so on until "Yishai begot David" — a righteous man, son of a righteous man — to inform us that it was not for nothing that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose David His servant, for there was a chain of ten completely righteous men, one above the other, resembling the ten orders of the world in the secret of the letter yod, for from Peretz to David there are ten levels, righteous man son of righteous man. Now consider the secret of what we have summarized in these words; and when you conduct yourself according to what we have informed you, I guarantee you that you will beget a righteous, pious son who sanctifies the Name of Heaven. Thus far the words of Ramban, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:114: Whoever does not marry a fitting wife and does not beget children is considered as dead (cf. Nedarim 64b), and whoever begets fitting children, even though he dies, is like one alive, as we learn in Bava Batra (116a): Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chama expounded, what is the meaning of what is written (1 Kings 11:21), "that David slept with his fathers," and "that Yoav, the general, died"? Why is "sleeping" said of David and "dying" of Yoav? David, who left behind a son, is spoken of with "sleeping"; Yoav, who left behind no son, is spoken of with "dying." But did Yoav leave no son? Is it not written, "and of the sons of Yoav, Ovadiah ben Yechiel"? Rather, David, who left behind a son like himself, is spoken of with "sleeping"; Yoav, who left behind no son like himself, is spoken of with "dying."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:1: Now that we have spoken of the holiness of the covenant, we must explain what blemishes it, and what its remedy would be. First we shall speak of the matter of emitting seed in vain, which is the most common, for there is scarcely a person in our generation who escapes it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:2: In tractate Niddah (13a) they were strict about the severity of this sin. These are their own words: Rabbi Eliezer says, whoever holds his member and urinates is as though he brought a flood upon the world. They said to Rabbi Eliezer, but sparks fly onto his feet and it appears as though he has crushed testicles [suggesting he cannot marry], and he thereby causes a slander to be spread about his children, that they are illegitimate. He said to them, better that a slander be spread about his children, that they are illegitimate, than that he make himself wicked for a single moment before the Omnipresent. It was taught in another version: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Sages, could a person perhaps stand in a high place and urinate, or urinate in loose earth, rather than make himself wicked for a single moment before the Omnipresent? Which did he say first? If you say the first version [about holding], he said it after having already stated the prohibition, [and then] he stated the remedy afterward — rather, he must have said this [about the high place] first. And they said to him: what if he has no high place or loose earth? He said to them, better that a slander be spread about his children than that he make himself wicked for a single moment before the Omnipresent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:3: And why all this? Because he thereby emits seed in vain — for Rabbi Yochanan said, whoever emits seed in vain is liable to death, as it is said (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and He put him to death also." Rabbi Yitzchak and Rabbi Ami said, it is as though he sheds blood, as it is said (Isaiah 57:5), "who inflame yourselves among the terebinths, under every leafy tree, who slaughter [shochtei] the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks" — do not read "shochtei" [slaughter] but "sochtei" [squeeze]. Rav Ashi said, it is as though he worships idols — here it is written, "under every leafy tree," and there it is written (Deuteronomy 12:2), "on the high mountains and under every leafy tree."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:4: And further it says below (13b): Rav said, whoever causes himself arousal deliberately shall be placed under a ban. Why did he not say it is forbidden? Because he thereby incites the evil inclination against himself. And Rabbi Ami said, he is called an apostate, for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him, do this and that; tomorrow it tells him, do such and such; the next day it tells him, go worship idols, and he goes and worships. Some say Rabbi Ami said, whoever brings himself to have a lustful fantasy is not admitted into the presence of the Holy One, blessed be He — here it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD," and there it is written (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You." And Rabbi Elazar said, what is the meaning of what is written (Isaiah 1:15), "your hands are full of blood"? These are the adulterers by hand. It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: "you shall not commit adultery" — there shall be no adultery in you, whether by hand or by foot. Our Rabbis taught: proselytes and those who play with children delay the coming of the Messiah, and they explained there in the Gemara that this refers to those who marry very young girls not yet able to bear children — for Rabbi Yosi said, the son of David will not come until all the souls in the [heavenly] Guf are exhausted, as it is said (Isaiah 57:16), "for the spirit would grow faint before Me, and the souls I have made." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:5: And in tractate Kallah (ch. 1) they said: Rabbi says, "who inflame yourselves among the terebinths" (Isaiah 57:5) — whoever heats himself up to emit seed in vain is considered like an animal: just as an animal is concerned only about slaughter and has no portion in the World to Come, so he has no portion in the World to Come. Of him Solomon said in his wisdom (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of man, whether it rises upward" — this refers to the souls of the righteous, who do not heat themselves up and do not emit seed in vain; "and the spirit of the animal, whether it descends downward to the earth" — this refers to the souls of the wicked, who heat themselves up and emit seed in vain. Whoever heats himself up [in this way] is liable to death, and whoever causes himself arousal is an apostate, as it is said (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD." Thus far his words.
